Administered wording and response anchor: “How affordable do you find your drinking water to be, considering the cost of buying cans or treating water … if any?” Very affordable; Somewhat affordable; Neutral; Somewhat unaffordable; Very unaffordable
Measurement rationale and alternatives: The broader two-item candidate showed weak coherence (rho=0.288, alpha=0.447). Q2.2 was retained as the primary measure. Value for money and the two-item mean remained alternatives.

Administered wording and response anchor: “How accessible is your primary drinking water supply …?” Very accessible; Accessible most of the time; Occasionally accessible; Rarely accessible; Not accessible
Measurement rationale and alternatives: The broader access family showed weak coherence (rho=0.203, alpha=0.433). Travel time, daily access time, and broader composites remained alternatives.

Administered wording and response anchor: “How often does your water supply face unexpected outages?” Never; Rarely; Occasionally; Frequently; Always
Measurement rationale and alternatives: Outage frequency was selected as the direct continuity deficit. Global reliability, timing, supply frequency, and outage duration capture related but distinct aspects of reliability.

Administered wording and response anchor: “How do you rate the efficiency of your primary water system? Efficiency here means the water system's ability to deliver sufficient water with minimal effort from the user, delay, or energy required to access it.” Very efficient; Efficient; Neutral; Inefficient; Very inefficient
Measurement rationale and alternatives: The broader candidate pair showed weak coherence (ho=0.245, alpha=0.393). Infrastructure maintenance remained a sensitivity measure.

Administered wording and response anchor: Appearance, taste, and odor, each rated Completely acceptable; Somewhat acceptable; Neutral; Somewhat unacceptable; Completely unacceptable
Final construction: Arithmetic mean of the three 1–5 items
Measurement rationale and alternatives: The three-item set showed coherent measurement (rho=0.533, alpha=0.774). Individual items and leave-one-out composites remained supporting checks.

Administered wording and response anchor: “How would you rate the quality of water you receive? Good quality water is defined as water in pristine condition and free from any known pollutants.” Excellent; Good; Neutral; Poor; Very poor
Measurement rationale and alternatives: Q7.1 was retained as the direct perceived-quality measure. Q12.2 safety trust was conceptually broader and remained an alternative.

Administered wording and response anchor: Sufficiency for daily needs, Always sufficient → Never sufficient; peak-time shortages, Never → Always
Final construction: Arithmetic mean after harmonizing both to a 1–5 worse-service direction
Measurement rationale and alternatives: Both items directly capture experienced quantity conditions (rho=0.356). Pressure and broader quantity composites remained alternatives.

Administered wording and response anchor: Complaint resolution, Always → Never; ease of reaching provider, Very easy → Very difficult, plus “No known stream of communication”
Final construction: Arithmetic mean of Q9.2 and harmonized Q9.3; raw Q9.3=6 mapped to harmonized 5
Measurement rationale and alternatives: The pair showed coherent measurement (rho=0.523, alpha=0.686). Global customer service, disruption notice, provider contact, and repair delay remained alternatives.
